summary: Charles Alexander Moore was a philosopher who earned his A.B. and Ph.D. at Yale University. He taught philosophy at Yale (~1933–1936), served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1936–1967), and founded and edited Philosophy East and West.

Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology, Charles B. Jones completed his PhD in History of Religions at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner in 1996. He held associate professor and associate dean roles at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).
Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at the University of Berlin (~1886–1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1913). He held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1893 to 1939.

Charles Burnett is a historian and philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and the Warburg Institute, where he became a lecturer in 1985 and professor in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey was a scholar of religious studies, history, and linguistics who studied under Theodor Nöldeke (~1891–1892). He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892–1900), served as professor at Yale University (1900–1932), and founded ASOR in 1901.

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned his dissertation at the University of Chicago. He chaired the Religious Studies Department at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (attested 1998–2006).
Charles DiSimone is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich in 2016 and held a post there in 2021.

Charles Duroiselle worked in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Indology. He founded the Burma Research Society (1910) and served as superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma (1912–1940) and as a professor at the University of Rangoon (~1920–1939).

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and historian who earned his BA, Ph.D., and D.Litt. from the University of London. He taught at SOAS (~1953–1959) and served as Archaeological Commissioner for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956–1967).

Charles Eliot was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Cheltenham College and Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Foreign Office (~1886–1926) and was principal of the University of Hong Kong (~1912–1918).
Charles Elliott was an Indologist who served in the East India Company from circa 1795 to 1827 and later held the post of treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1837–1856).

Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School (~1892–1896). Working in ethnology and archaeology, he held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard. He held a post as associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who earned his B.D. and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago (~1956–1974), UNC Chapel Hill and Duke (~1974–1987), Syracuse (~1987–1991), and UC Santa Barbara (~1991–1996).

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 1988). He held professorial posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1988–1992), Harvard (1996–2001, 2007), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2001, 2005).

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as principal of Presidency College, Chennai (1876–1892), head of Presidency University (1875–1892), and librarian of the India Office Library (1892–1903).

Charles Li is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020) and held a post at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2023).

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held posts at the University of Lyon (~1967–1972) and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1998).
Charles Oman was a historian and archaeologist who studied at New College (~1878–1883). He subsequently held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1905 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1883–1886). He later held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1917 to 1935.
